title: Functorial bounded derived-tensor Tor spectral sequence
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $C,D\in D^b(R)$, the bounded subcategory [def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories] of the cochain derived category of $R$-modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Use the ordinary K-flat derived tensor $C\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}D$ of [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor] with $A=R$, and the Tor groups of [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules], extended by zero in negative homological degrees. There is a cohomological spectral sequence $E_s^{p,q}(C,D)$, $s\ge2$, in $R$-modules [def-sp-spectral-sequence], with
$$E_2^{p,q}(C,D)=\bigoplus_{i+j=q}\operatorname{Tor}_{-p}^R(H^i(C),H^j(D)),\qquad d_s:E_s^{p,q}\longrightarrow E_s^{p+s,q-s+1}.$$
For every integer $n$ it converges with a finite decreasing filtration $F^pH^n(C\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}D)$ [def-sp-filtration] and canonical identifications
$$F^pH^n/F^{p+1}H^n\cong E_\infty^{p,n-p}.$$
Here $E_\infty^{p,q}$ is the stationary value of the pages at $(p,q)$. The spectral sequence, the abutment filtration and these identifications are functorial in both derived-category arguments: morphisms $u:C\to C'$ and $v:D\to D'$ induce compatible page maps, on $E_2$ the direct sums of $\operatorname{Tor}_{-p}^R(H^i(u),H^j(v))$, and on the abutment $H^n(u\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}v)$, preserving $F^p$. No finite generation or finite global dimension of $R$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0H7Z, lemma-kunneth-spectral-sequence; Tag 0H7Y, proposition-kunneth-filtered, and the construction in section-kunneth-spectral-sequence. Functorial version of the canonical truncation-filtration construction. Read existing cache /home/ubuntu/c1-stacks-review/more-algebra.tex, lines 15420–15832; tags verified in tags/tags.

proof.text:
Choose bounded cochain representatives $K,L$ of $C,D$. Explicitly, if the cohomology of a representative $V$ is supported in $[c,d]$, first replace $V$ by $\tau_{\le d}V$ (cycles in degree $d$, zero above), then quotient by the subcomplex having the old terms below $c$, $\operatorname{im}(d^{c-1})$ in degree $c$, and zero above. The resulting bounded complex has the same cohomology: the removed lower subcomplex is acyclic and upper truncation preserves all nonzero cohomology. This is the canonical truncation construction in [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category], using the cohomology convention in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].
Put $F^iK=\tau_{\le -i}K$ and $F^jL=\tau_{\le -j}L$. These filtrations are finite as complexes because $K,L$ are bounded termwise. For $m=-i$, the quotient $\tau_{\le m}K/\tau_{\le m-1}K$ is the two-term complex $\operatorname{im}(d^{m-1})\hookrightarrow\ker(d^m)$ in degrees $m-1,m$. Projection from cycles to cohomology is therefore a natural quasi-isomorphism
$$\operatorname{gr}^i_F K\longrightarrow H^{-i}(C)[i].$$
The identical construction gives $\operatorname{gr}^j_F L\to H^{-j}(D)[j]$. The quotient maps commute with every chain map because a chain map preserves cycles and boundaries.

proof.text: Apply [lem-kun-finite-filtered-kflat-replacement] to each of the finite filtered complexes $(K,F)$ and $(L,F)$ of Step 1. Obtain filtered quasi-isomorphisms $P\to K$ and $Q\to L$, with finite filtrations and with underlying, step and graded complexes K-flat and all their terms flat. Its equivalence after localization says that these replacements may be used for morphisms and equality of morphisms as well as for objects. In particular the canonical graded identifications of Step 1 apply to $P,Q$ in $D(R)$. The resolution complexes need not be bounded in their cochain degrees; only their filtrations must be finite.

source.place: Tag 0H7X, lemma-resolution-filtered-complex, applied to the finite canonical truncation filtrations; finite-interval/roof form

proof.text:
Give $T=\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_R Q)$ its convolution filtration $G$. By [lem-kun-filtered-tensor-graded-comparison] it is finitely filtered, represents the ordinary derived tensor $C\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}D$, and has
$$\operatorname{gr}^a_G T\cong\bigoplus_{i+j=a}\operatorname{gr}^iP\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}\operatorname{gr}^jQ.$$
To meet the hypothesis of [lem-sp-bounded-filtered-page-core] for every finitely filtered complex $(U,F)$, define $\varphi(U,a,t):F^aU/F^{a+t}U\to F^{a-t+1}U/F^{a+1}U$ by sending the class of $x$ to the class of the same $x$. It is well-defined for $t\ge1$ because $F^{a+t}\subseteq F^{a+1}$ and $F^a\subseteq F^{a-t+1}$. Its composite with the source projection is the filtration inclusion followed by the target projection, as required. This construction applies in particular to $(T,G)$. The cited theorem gives a spectral sequence $E'$ beginning on page one, with differentials $(a,b)\mapsto(a+t,b-t+1)$ and
$$ (E')_1^{a,b}\cong\bigoplus_{i+j=a}H^{a+b}\bigl(\operatorname{gr}^iP\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}\operatorname{gr}^jQ\bigr).$$
More explicitly, choose integer filtration bounds $A_P<B_P$ and $A_Q<B_Q$ with $F^{A_P}P=P$, $F^{B_P}P=0$, $F^{A_Q}Q=Q$, and $F^{B_Q}Q=0$. Put $A=A_P+A_Q$ and $B=B_P+B_Q-1$. Then $G^AT=T$, since the summand with $(i,j)=(A_P,A_Q)$ is all of $T$, and $G^BT=0$, since $i+j=B$ forces $i\ge B_P$ or $j\ge B_Q$. In particular the old pages have zero terms outside columns $A\le a<B$. Only finitely many graded pairs $i,j$ can contribute. Cohomology of this finite direct sum is the direct sum of cohomologies, since its cycles and boundaries are the corresponding finite sums. The theorem also gives the finite image filtration $G^aH^n(T)=\operatorname{im}(H^n(G^aT)\to H^n(T))$, stabilization at each bidegree, and stationary-page identifications with its successive quotients.

proof.text:
For modules $M,N$ in degree zero choose a free resolution $A_\bullet\to M$ as allowed in [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules], and place $A_s$ in cochain degree $-s$. A free module is flat: tensoring with $\bigoplus_I R$ is $\bigoplus_I$ of the original sequence, whose kernels and images are computed coordinatewise on finite-support vectors. Thus this nonpositive free complex is K-flat by [lem-pc-module-bounded-flat-kflat]. By [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor] its tensor with $N$ computes $M\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}N$. The Tor definition gives $H^{-s}(M\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}N)=\operatorname{Tor}^R_s(M,N)$ for $s\ge0$, and positive cochain degrees vanish. These identifications are natural: for a module map $\phi:M\to M\prime$, choose a free-resolution lift as follows. In degree zero lift the images of basis vectors through the target augmentation. Inductively, the required image of the boundary of a basis vector is a cycle in the target resolution; exactness gives a preimage in its next degree, and extend these choices linearly. After this lift, the maps on Tor and on tensor homology agree by [lem-weil-pbc-tor-map-via-resolution-lift]; in the second variable the chain map is $1\otimes v$ as in that node.
The total tensor convention [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] gives $(A[i]\otimes B[j])\cong(A\otimes B)[i+j]$: on an element originally of first-factor degree $k$, multiply by $(-1)^{jk}$. For the first differential the two signs agree because $j(k+1)=jk+j$; for the second they agree because $i$ and $-i$ have the same parity. This is natural in both factors. Applying these computations and Step 1 to Step 3 yields
$$ (E')_1^{a,b}\cong\bigoplus_{i+j=a}\operatorname{Tor}_{-2a-b}^R(H^{-i}(C),H^{-j}(D)).$$
Here a negative Tor index denotes zero; no global-dimension bound is used.

proof.text:
For $s\ge2$, set $E_s^{p,q}=(E')_{s-1}^{-q,p+2q}$. This is an invertible change of bidegrees, with inverse $(a,b)\mapsto(p,q)=(b+2a,-a)$; it preserves total degree since $a+b=p+q$. With $(a,b)=(-q,p+2q)$, the differential on page $s-1$ goes to
$$(a',b')=(-q+s-1,p+2q-s+2).$$
Its new indices are $q'=-a'=q-s+1$ and $p'=b'+2a'=p+s$, as required. The successor-page homology isomorphism of $E'$ is carried to the successor-page isomorphism of $E$ at the same changed bidegree, so this is a spectral sequence in the sense of [def-sp-spectral-sequence]. At $s=2$ the index in Step 4 is $-2(-q)-(p+2q)=-p$; putting $I=-i$, $J=-j$ changes $i+j=-q$ to $I+J=q$. Hence
$$E_2^{p,q}=\bigoplus_{I+J=q}\operatorname{Tor}_{-p}^R(H^I(C),H^J(D)).$$
The isomorphisms with this displayed page are the canonical ones from Steps 1, 3 and 4 (one may conjugate the page-two differential by these isomorphisms).

proof.text:
For a fixed total degree $n$, $q=n-p$ and therefore the old filtration index is $a=-q=p-n$. Define the asserted decreasing filtration by
$$F^pH^n(C\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}D)=G^{p-n}H^n(T).$$
It is finite by Step 3, in the sense of [def-sp-filtration]. The graded identification there gives
$$F^pH^n/F^{p+1}H^n\cong(E')_\infty^{p-n,\,2n-p}=E_\infty^{p,n-p}.$$
The bounds $A,B$ from Step 3 give an explicit stabilization check: on every old page $t\ge B-A$, a differential from a supported column $a$ lands in column $a+t\ge B$, and a differential into it originates in column $a-t<A$. Both vanish; the successor-page homology maps are therefore isomorphisms. Thus all new pages are stationary once $s\ge B-A+1$, independently of $n$. Equivalently, their support is in the finite horizontal strip $-B<q\le -A$. This does not require any bound in the other bidegree. This is precisely the asserted convergence and finite filtration. In particular finite filtration length does not assert bounded cohomology of the derived tensor: there can be infinitely many nonzero Tor degrees.

proof.text: The canonical filtrations of Step 1 extend to all bounded derived morphisms by [lem-kun-derived-canonical-filtration]. Apply its functor separately to $C$ and $D$, and compose with the localized convolution tensor of [lem-kun-filtered-tensor-localization]. For the chosen bounded representatives and good replacements of Steps 1--3 this composite is represented by $(T,G)$. Thus a pair $u:C\to C'$, $v:D\to D'$ gives a morphism of finite filtered localized complexes; its underlying derived morphism is $u\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}v$, and its degree-$a$ graded map is the sum of the derived tensors of $H^{-i}(u)[i]$ and $H^{-j}(v)[j]$, $i+j=a$. Both cited results are functorial in all localized morphisms, so identities, composition and interchange already hold.

source.place: Tags 0H7X/0H7Y/0H7Z: canonical truncation filtration, convolution tensor, and localization; extracted descent interfaces replace the first two paragraphs of returned Step 7.

proof.text: Apply [lem-kun-filtered-page-localization] to the morphism of Step 7. It supplies compatible old page maps, the cohomology map $H^n(u\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}v)$, maps preserving every image-filtration step $G^aH^n$, and natural isomorphisms from the stationary old pages to the quotients $G^aH^n/G^{a+1}H^n$. Take these image-normalized comparisons as the canonical identifications $F^pH^n/F^{p+1}H^n\cong E_\infty^{p,n-p}$ of Step 6 (after the relabelling of Step 9); Step 3 is used only for the existence of the stationary pages and of the finite image filtration, not for a second choice of identification. Their compatibility with the successor-page maps ensures that choosing a later stationary page leaves the identifications compatible. All these maps satisfy functor laws because the cited result factors the entire construction through the filtered localization.

source.place: Tags 012M/012O/012P/012W: descent, filtered abutment and stationary comparison naturality extracted from returned Step 7.

proof.text: The Tor-resolution identifications and the natural signed shift map in Step 4 identify the page-one maps of Step 8 with the direct sums of the induced Tor maps. Indeed the graded morphisms are the cohomology maps shifted by $i,j$ by Step 7; after the sign isomorphism their tensor-homology maps are exactly the two resolution formulas of [lem-weil-pbc-tor-map-via-resolution-lift]. Relabel these maps by Step 5, so at page two they are $\bigoplus_{I+J=q}\operatorname{Tor}_{-p}^R(H^I(u),H^J(v))$. Finally relabel the filtration maps and stationary quotient comparisons by $a=p-n$ as in Step 6. The underlying abutment map remains $H^n(u\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}v)$ and the graded map is at $(p,n-p)$. These substitutions preserve the commuting squares from Step 8. This proves all functoriality clauses of the unchanged statement.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q95-16b8f1518 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the full repair of the returned step 7. Steps 1-6, the statement, stmt_deps and the Lean record are byte-identical to the live side copy; the live node is unsplit, so this delivery is admissible. Steps 7-9 cite the three new statement-only nodes and the Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-tor-map-via-resolution-lift, and each step uses exactly what those statements say. I re-checked the index arithmetic: E'_1 Tor index -2a-b = -p, the d_s bidegree (s,1-s), and F^p = G^{p-n}. The Z/2 (x) Z/2 case gives the expected E_2 terms. I checked the sources at Stacks more-algebra.tex lines 15645-15835 (0H7X, 0H7Y, 0H7Z) and the tags 0H7W, 0118, 05RW, 05S1, 05S2, 05S6, 012M, 012O, 012P, 012W; tags and labels agree. The coefficient category is ordinary R-modules with the K-flat derived tensor, the same as the unchanged statement; no base-change morphism is involved, and no SGA source is used. All three new nodes are true and none restates a clause of the item. (1) derived-canonical-filtration: tau-filtrations of bounded complexes are finite, chain homotopies preserve them, and quasi-isomorphisms become graded quasi-isomorphisms (gr^i = H^{-i}[i]), so the functor factors through K^b[qis^-1] = D^b(R). (2) filtered-tensor-localization: convolution of good complexes is good and preserves graded quasi-isomorphisms (by the graded-comparison node); the two explicit homotopy formulas are filtered; transport is along the K-flat replacement equivalence. (3) filtered-page-localization: by finite induction a graded quasi-isomorphism is one on every step; for t >= B-A the page equals im(H^n(F^a) -> H^n(U/F^{a+1})), which is isomorphic to I^a/I^{a+1} by the kernel computation, with the stated normalization. I tested the zero ring, one-step filtrations, M[0], an acyclic two-step complex and Z/2. The rg duplicate sweep found nothing that states these interfaces for an arbitrary commutative R with unbounded cochain degrees; the closest candidates were lem-trf-filtered-operations-hom (etale, finite-Tor), lem-trf-finite-filtered-flat-resolution (bounded above, acyclicity only), lem-trf-filtered-bounded-localization-comparison, lem-trf-filtered-unbounded-truncation, lem-trf-filtered-bifunctor-graded-comparison, def-sp-filtered-complex-decalage and lem-sp-bounded-filtered-page-core. Each new node carries five searches, a correct blueprint from/via, and created.item set to the item. Tool uses accepted again: lem-sp-bounded-filtered-page-core, lem-pc-module-bounded-flat-kflat and lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor, all unchanged and no new off-unit citation.
